messages:
Alice: quick q about async job handshake + cancel semantics for /v1/jobs — trying to lock down the contract before the SDK changes. If a client polls and then gives up (abort), do we expect the server to keep the job running? Or should abort implicitly cancel? cc @Ben @Chandra

Ben: short answer: we should not silently cancel on client abort. client abort != server cancel. we need an explicit cancel endpoint (DELETE /v1/jobs/:id) or a cancel request so server-side work isn't torn down unexpectedly. :thumbsup:

Chandra: agree. also we need to clarify race when cancel + completion happen close together. propose states: queued -> running -> cancelling -> cancelled | completed | failed. in the race, server should transition to completed if final output already persisted, otherwise to cancelled. we should surface a "final_state_reason" string in the status to help debugging.

Alice: sounds good. Ben — is there an existing cancel flow in runtime? devops/runtime behavior matters because we may not be able to preempt some GPU jobs.

Ben: runtime: we enqueue a cancel request to the worker; worker tries graceful shutdown for N=30s grace then force-stop. for long-running ops that aren't checkpointable we mark cancelled but may still finish compute — we'll mark final_state_reason="completed-after-cancel-request" if output was produced. we should be explicit in docs.

Eva: question re: polling response shape backwards compat: current schema is minimal: {"id":"..","status":"running","result":null}. can we add optional fields (progress, eta, cancelable, expires_at) without breaking clients?

Chandra: yes opt-in. add fields as optional. but call out that some SDKs may validate strictly; we should bump API minor and announce. suggested poll schema snippet: 

```json
{
  "id": "job_abc123",
  "status": "running",        // queued | running | cancelling | cancelled | completed | failed
  "progress": 0.42,           // optional float
  "eta_seconds": 35,          // optional
  "cancelable": true,         // optional bool
  "expires_at": "2026-08-12T15:04:05Z", // optional poll-token expiry
  "result": null,
  "final_state_reason": null // optional string for race/cancel details
}
```

Ben: +1. also add a short-lived poll token TTL (default 5m) so we can GC stale jobs and avoid infinite polling pain. token expiry should be orthogonal to job lifetime. if token expired, poll returns 410 with a hint to re-query or re-start job.

Alice: 410 instead of 404? ok. 410 sounds good to indicate resource gone / token invalid. what's the suggested client flow on 410? auto re-submit or ask user?

Chandra: return header 'Retry-After' and body with reason. recommend SDKs surface a RetryableError with code 'POLL_TOKEN_EXPIRED' so apps can choose to re-submit or surface an error. document recommended approach: if job is idempotent and you have request_id, re-submit; otherwise prompt user.

devbot: buildbot: PR created -> https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4827 (api: async job schema + cancel endpoint)

Eva: small nit — cancel endpoint semantics: should it be idempotent? i.e., repeated DELETE calls should return 202 if cancel in progress, 204 if already cancelled/completed?

Ben: yes idempotent. recommended codes: 202 Accepted when transition to cancelling queued; 204 No Content if already cancelled; 409 Conflict if cannot cancel (e.g., immutable archived job) with body explaining why.

Alice: ok plan: Ben will update runtime doc + implement server responses. Chandra will draft API markdown (include schema snippet above + error codes). Eva will add SDK error class + tests for 410 handling. I'll open follow-up RFC with timeline. thanks all :raised_hands:

Ben: I'll add a short example curl for cancel semantics:

```bash
# request cancel
curl -X DELETE -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/jobs/job_abc123"
# server responses:
# 202 {"status":"cancelling"}
# 204 (already cancelled)
# 409 {"error":"cannot_cancel","reason":"archived"}
```

Chandra: I'll add note about final_state_reason values ("timeout","preempted","completed-after-cancel-request","client-requested") and include examples in RFC.

Alice: great. can we aim to merge API docs this week? I'll call out potential SDK breaking only if clients strictly validate. otherwise should be backward compatible.

Eva: yes aiming for EOD Friday. will add tests. :eyes:

devbot: reminder: rollout checklist — include migration guide and changelog entry.

Alice: thanks everyone — closing thread, will follow up in the RFC PR.
